source_note: Curated from AARP, Cleveland Clinic, Kaiser Permanente, and NIA-style geriatric guidance. Low-intensity, knee-aware. MUST be reviewed with your care team before use; this is a starting template, not medical advice.

exercises.name: Ankle Pumps
steps: Sit tall with both feet flat on the floor.
Lift your toes toward you while keeping your heels down, then press your toes down and lift your heels.
Pump slowly and steadily, about 15 times.
This keeps the blood moving in your lower legs.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — no change needed.
exercises.safetyCue: Keep the motion at the ankles. Easy and rhythmic, no straining.

exercises.name: Seated Straight-Leg Lifts
steps: Sit tall with your back supported and feet flat.
Straighten one leg until it is roughly parallel with the floor, or as close as is comfortable.
Hold for a few seconds, then lower slowly.
Do about 10 on each leg, alternating.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — gentle on the knee.
exercises.safetyCue: Lift only to a comfortable height. Lower with control rather than dropping the leg.

exercises.name: Shoulder Blade Squeezes
steps: Sit tall with arms relaxed and shoulders down.
Gently draw your shoulder blades together, as if holding a pencil between them.
Hold for 3 to 5 seconds, then release.
Repeat about 10 times. Good for posture.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — no change needed.
exercises.safetyCue: Keep shoulders down away from your ears. Squeeze gently, don't shrug.

exercises.name: Overhead Arm Reach
steps: Sit tall with feet flat.
Slowly raise both arms up overhead as far as is comfortable.
Reach gently toward the ceiling, then lower the arms with control.
Repeat about 8 times.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — no change needed.
exercises.safetyCue: Only raise as high as your shoulders allow without pain. Keep breathing.

exercises.name: Heel Raises
steps: Stand behind a sturdy chair, holding the back for support.
Slowly rise up onto the balls of your feet, lifting your heels.
Hold for a moment, then lower slowly.
Repeat about 10 times.
exercises.seatedVariant: Seated: with feet flat, press through the balls of your feet to lift your heels, then lower. About 12 times.
exercises.safetyCue: Keep a hand on the chair. Rise only as high as feels steady.

exercises.name: Standing Side Leg Raises
steps: Stand behind a sturdy chair, holding on with both hands.
Keeping your leg straight and your body tall, lift one leg out to the side a few inches.
Lower it slowly with control.
Do about 8 on each side.
exercises.seatedVariant: Seated: slide one foot out to the side along the floor and back, keeping the leg relaxed. About 10 each side.
exercises.safetyCue: Keep both hands on the chair and your torso upright. Lift only a small amount.

exercises.name: Side-to-Side Weight Shifts
steps: Stand behind a sturdy chair with feet about hip-width apart, hands on the back.
Slowly shift your weight onto your right foot, feeling your balance settle.
Then shift smoothly onto your left foot.
Continue gently side to side, about 10 shifts each way.
exercises.seatedVariant: Seated: gently lean your weight from one hip to the other, side to side, about 10 each way.
exercises.safetyCue: Keep the shifts small and controlled, hands resting on the chair.

exercises.name: Seated Side Bends
steps: Sit tall with feet flat and hands resting on your thighs.
Reach your right arm up and gently lean to the left, feeling a stretch along your right side.
Return to center, then reach your left arm up and lean right.
Repeat 5 times each way.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — no change needed.
exercises.safetyCue: Lean only until you feel a mild stretch. Keep both hips on the chair.

exercises.name: Wrist Circles & Hand Opens
steps: Rest your forearms on your thighs or the armrests.
Slowly circle both wrists 8 times one way, then 8 the other.
Then open your hands wide, spreading the fingers, and close into a soft fist.
Repeat the open-and-close about 10 times.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — no change needed.
exercises.safetyCue: Gentle and slow; stop if any joint feels sore.

exercises.name: Seated Deep Breathing
steps: Sit tall and comfortable, shoulders relaxed, hands on your belly.
Breathe in slowly through your nose, feeling your belly rise, for a count of 4.
Breathe out gently through pursed lips for a count of 6.
Repeat for about 6 slow breaths.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — no change needed.
exercises.safetyCue: Keep it easy and unhurried. If you feel lightheaded, return to normal breathing.
